text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures remain firm but U.S. cash market outpaces German paper after U.S. April retail sales data show 0.3 drop on month -- in line with forecasts. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.18, down 0.09 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts shed early gains as profit-takers moved in, while the softer tone in U.S. Treasuries also dampened sentiment. Gilts earlier moved higher after the Bank of England said further tightening of monetary policy was needed. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 114-11/32, down 03/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond future fails to hold gains above 130.40 after U.S. retail sales and settles marginally higher. Await CSA opinion poll due 1700 GMT but little reaction expected unless sharp swing to left as belief in centre-right victory growing. Franc also benefitting, at strongest vs mark since April 18. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.38 up 0.08 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures drifted lower in late afternoon following lower T-bonds after U.S. retail April retail sales had initially pushed Treasuries higher. BTPs cautious ahead of Italian government's three-year economic plan expected later this month and details of the 1998 deficit-cutting budget. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.59 down 0.13 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Treasuries mostly remain in the minus column. Longs "sold the news" after brief pop on 0.3 pct Apr retail sales drop. Mixed Richmond, Atlanta fed reports seen not key for bonds. PPI, CPI Wed and Thurs seen friendly for bonds but upside seen limited--data discounted. 2-yr note toppish at 6.20 pct.The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-02/32, down 10/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.9 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended sharply higher as investor buying of cash JGBs prompted dealers to cover short positions in late afternoon trade. Short-covering in June increasing ahead of expected roll forward of benchmark futures contract, traders said.In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.12, up 0.92 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market had one of its busier mornings of late with a string of chunky dollar deals emerging on Tuesday. BT launched a $1.0 billion 10-year bond, hot on the heels of a successful $1.5 billion five-year in April. A Toyota unit set a $400 million five-year bond. Wachovia Bank issued a $350 million five-year FRN. Nestle brought a $300 million five-year convertible. Mexico is planning a 300 million stg five-year Eurobond.
